newsitem.title: UK: LME lead and zinc end firmer, others lose steam.
newsitem.headline: LME lead and zinc end firmer, others lose steam.

text.p: LME metals deflated in afternoon activity as the day's market leaders zinc and lead drifted off fresh peaks while others settled back into well-worn ranges.
Zinc finished the afternoon kerb $6 higher at $1,296 after earlier steaming to a fresh 4-1/2 year peak at $1,307.
A short-term correction may be on the cards since momentum indicators were showing an overbought market, with the 14-day RSI rising to around 77, analysts said.
"If it does dip, though, it should be very well bought by people who need to hedge and cover," said analyst Helen Williamson of broker Brandeis.

In the medium term, rising prices should continue, analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said. "The steady uptrend is enjoying an accelerated phase...there are no signs of the uptrend being threatened yet," she said.
The medium term target was around $1,400, she added.
Lead also floated off a peak of $710 touched in the morning, ending the day at $704, up $14.

The market scored the highest levels in nearly two months largely on fund short-covering and Far Eastern buying linked to option positions, but the lacklustre physical market has not improved, traders said.
Prices may try higher in the short-term towards resistance at $710 and $725, but would unlikely be able to sustain the higher levels, Williamson said.
Support was pegged around $685/7, based on Thursday's and Friday's lows as well as the 10-day moving average, and then $674, chartists said.
Copper made a stab higher early in the morning to $2,379 but lost steam and probed negative territory in the afternoon, unable to break out of its recent range.
The cash/threes backwardation initially flared, but ended a touch narrower at $43/$48.
Aluminium kept to a narrow range, consolidating in its recent $1,650-$1,690 price band. It closed the day unchanged at $1,668 per tonne.
Nickel failed to sustain higher levels achieved in the morning when it touched $8,l75, slumping to end the kerb $75 lower at $8,040.
Tin finished $5 weaker at $6,055 and alloy lost $5 to $1,545.
